records.name: California
records.summary: Highest legal floor in the country: the first sanctuary-state law for transgender care (SB 107, signed 2022) and shield protections against out-of-state enforcement. But also the most recorded incidents of any state in 2025 (198, GLAAD ALERT), a "dramatic increase" in Los Angeles hate-crime reports, and 34 recorded killings of trans women 2008–2025 (4.1 per 100k). Above the national score 0.36; law and street volume pull opposite ways.

sources.summary: GLAAD ALERT Desk documented more than 1,000 anti-LGBTQ incidents nationwide in 2025; states with the most: California (198), New Hampshire (72), Texas (66), Ohio (50), Washington (50).

Analysis of 2025 incident data: California recorded the most incidents of any state (198), and law-enforcement data shows 'a dramatic increase' in anti-LGBTQ hate-crime reports in Los Angeles during the same period as Gov. Gavin Newsom's platforming of anti-trans figures.

July 2026 analysis: California falls in the 'Safest States' law band (score 4.1) with 1.9 recorded incidents - the piece argues even the most protective law floors do not eliminate recorded hostility.

Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 107 (September 2022), making California the first sanctuary state for transgender youth seeking care: out-of-state youth can access hormones and puberty blockers here, and the law shields families from child-abuse investigations or criminal prosecution for seeking gender-affirming care.

records.name: Colorado
records.summary:
Anti-discrimination law here expressly covers gender identity and gender expression in employment, housing and public accommodation, the last directly traveller-relevant for hotels, restaurants and venues, and the state's highest court enforced that coverage in May 2026 by ordering a hospital to resume the youth gender-affirming care it had suspended under national pressure. A July 2026 national risk map lists this state among the country's most protective, citing insurance-coverage mandates and refuge protections for people fleeing restrictive laws elsewhere.

The 2025 national document and passport restrictions apply here as across the country.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (403); the underlying source is the Colorado Legislature's 2025 summary of gender-affirming-care and transgender legislation (r25-595), documenting that CADA's non-discrimination coverage — employment, housing and public accommodations, expressly including gender identity and gender expression — was expanded again in 2025.

July 2026 assessment lists Colorado among 'Most Protective States (CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MA, MD, MN, NJ...)'; the page also counts Colorado among states with comprehensive health-insurance laws covering facial-hair removal and expanded gender-related coverage, and among the top states for trans people seeking security.

The Colorado Supreme Court ruled 5-2 on May 18, 2026 that Children's Hospital Colorado violated the state's anti-discrimination law when it suspended gender-affirming care for transgender youth under federal pressure, and ordered a lower court to issue an injunction requiring the hospital to resume the care (puberty blockers, hormone therapy). Justice William Hood wrote that continuing such treatment for cisgender children while stopping it for transgender youth meant the decision 'denies petitioners the full and equal enjoyment of services based on gender identity'; two justices dissented, citing federal threats that could shut the hospital system. The ruling documents Colorado's highest court actively enforcing the gender-identity protections on which this record's anti-discrimination claim rests.

Colorado voters will decide in November 2026 whether to ban transgender kids from gendered sports that do not align with their biological sex (Initiative 109) and to prohibit surgery on a child for the purpose of altering their sex characteristics (Initiative 110), after state elections officials certified the voter signatures on the three measures including Initiative 108 on child sex trafficking (The Colorado Sun, Mar. 17, 2026). The initiatives were pushed by conservative activists and would, if passed, write restrictions on transgender minors into state law. They are the first statewide ballot-level counter-pressure to Colorado's protective legal posture that this record documents.

Colorado will suspend Medicaid coverage for hormone therapy, puberty blockers and other gender-affirming care for transgender youth beginning Oct. 13, 2026, because a new federal rule finalized in August 2026 blocks federal funds for such care for people under 18 (and under 19 under the CHP+ child program); the state's Medicaid agency said resuming coverage 'will require legislative action' (The Colorado Sun, Aug. 21, 2026). About 500 youth under 19 received Medicaid-covered hormone therapy for gender dysphoria in fiscal 2024-25, and patients already taking hormones keep coverage through a six-month tapering period while behavioural healthcare is unaffected. The suspension shows Colorado's protections operating under direct federal-funding pressure, relevant to a trans visitor's assessment of the state.
